URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/13/trump-xi-summit-chinas-help-in-iran-may-require-us-concessions

China has been "reluctant to get involved in the crisis" — analyst Christopher Heurlin. Beijing recently hosted Iran's foreign minister but appears to be "waiting for this visit" before applying pressure on Tehran.

Professor Inderjeet Parmar: China may seek "opposition to Taiwanese independence" as leverage for Iran assistance.

Heurlin: Beijing wants Trump to block a "$14bn" weapons package to Taiwan currently on his desk.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged China to "join us in supporting this international operation" to reopen Hormuz passage. However, approaches diverge: Trump relies on military threats while China advocates restraint and diplomacy.

China is the "top importer of Iranian oil" and faces economic strain from the disruption. Beijing has "amassed oil reserves" that help buffer shortages, but these resources remain "finite," creating incentive to restore shipping lanes.

Summit Agenda: Taiwan remains China's "top issue," while Trump will likely push Beijing to purchase more U.S. agricultural products. Analyst view: "Iran is not really the central issue for either party."
